subject: Beta model and Poisson prior on one Beta parameter

messages.author: 26c971075f8aedcc
messages.subject: Beta model and Poisson prior on one Beta parameter
parts:
Hi,

I would like to fit this model:

r ~ Poisson(lambda) # lambda is known
l_i ~ Beta(1.0, r) # for a range of values

My attempt at this with R interface to Stan was:

Model <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real<lower=0, upper=1> l[N];
  real<lower=0> lambda;
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> r;
}

model {
  # r ~ poisson(lambda);
  increment_log_prob(poisson_log(r, lambda));
  for (j in 1:n) {
    l[j] ~ beta(1.0, r);
  }
}
"
Segments <- c(0.1, 0.5, 0.4)
Lambda <- 1.0
Data <- list(N=length(Segments), l=Segments, Lambda=Lambda)

Output <- stan(model_code=Model, data=Data, chains=3,
                   warmup=500, iter=1500,seed =19791123)

but I get the following error due to r being real:

Error in stanc(file, model_name = model_name, model_code = model_code,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'Model' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

No matches for: 

  poisson_log(real, real)

Available argument signatures for poisson_log:

  poisson_log(int, real)
  poisson_log(int, real[])
  poisson_log(int, vector)
  poisson_log(int, row vector)
  poisson_log(int[], real)
  poisson_log(int[], real[])
  poisson_log(int[], vector)
  poisson_log(int[], row vector)


ERROR at line 14

 12:    model {
 13:      # r ~ poisson(lambda);
 14:      increment_log_prob(poisson_log(r, lambda));
                                                   ^
 15:      for (j in 1:n) {

Any suggestions?

Thanks!

Regards, Gregor

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: Beta model and Poisson prior on one Beta parameter
parts: You cannot have discrete parameters in your model as Stan uses HMC, which requires a continuous parameter space. For some models that do have discrete parameters, you can marginalize over the possible values for the discrete parameter, provided that they constitute a limited set (or can be assumed to be). See Stan manual chapter on mixture models. Manual in general is a good place to start reading up on HMC.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Beta model and Poisson prior on one Beta parameter
parts:
How about

r ~ normal(lambda,sqrt(lambda));

That matches the first two moments given that you say lambda
is known. The parameter r for the beta distribution is continuous
anyway.

- Bob

parts:
I think you’ll want a gamma to match the positivity needed
for the beta parameters (as Bob notes it’s real anyways).
You can play around with the two parameters of the gamma
to ensure that the mean and variance match.

constrain it to be positive, the moments won't match because of the
truncation! It'll get close for lambda > 10 or so, but that's not the
same.

- Bob
